source.title: Why flatness does and does not correlate with generalization for deep neural networks
source.authors: Shuo Zhang; Isaac Reid; Guillermo Valle Pérez; A. Louis

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper and appendices; no material cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses function-prior measurements and sharpness correlations to test whether flatness tracks the training–test generalization gap, including across optimizers and parameter rescaling.
record.gate_note: The attack-set experiments deliberately train on incorrectly labelled examples while retaining zero training error, then measure test error, prior and sharpness. The paper’s main measured results are about prior and flatness correlations, not natural-label versus random-label generalization. Boolean-system flatness/prior results do not measure generalization because the full input space is evaluated. Values in the correlation plots are not numerically reported in text, so rows record the authors’ explicit qualitative descriptions. Cited findings from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Section 5.3 reports that Adam and plain SGD have similar held-out performance with default TensorFlow hyperparameters, bearing on V4 in simplified image tasks with attack sets. The extracted sharpness correlations do not test V7's specified magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance; Appendix A.2 explicitly distinguishes the measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the tested local flatness measures sometimes correlate with generalization, but optimizer changes and parameter rescaling can disrupt the relationship; estimated log P(f) is more robust in these experiments. This conclusion does not establish failure of V7's distinct magnitude-aware measure.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures Keskar-style sharpness and Hessian-based flatness alongside Bayesian function-prior correlations, using an attack-set procedure to vary generalization. It does not reproduce V7’s magnitude-aware perturbation measure or compare against its stated norm- and margin-based measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Flatness–generalization correlation changes with optimizer: broken for Adam and Entropy-SGD on FCN/MNIST and Adam on FCN/CIFAR-10; less deterioration for Adam on ResNet50/CIFAR-10; also broken for Adagrad, Momentum, and RMSProp but similar to vanilla SGD for full-batch gradient descent. Sharpness values change over training and depend on its calculation hyperparameters. Parameter rescaling changes sharpness while leaving the represented function initially unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss-sharpness correlations are scattered under vanilla SGD, deteriorate under several optimizers, and remain similar during overtraining; Hessian-based metrics show analogous behavior.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these attack-set classification experiments, the association between local loss flatness and test error depends on the optimizer and measure.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated log function prior tracks test error more consistently than the tested local flatness metrics across optimizer changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Estimated log P(f) predicts test error robustly across the tested classification tasks and optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter rescaling changes local sharpness while initially preserving the represented function; continued training can lower sharpness without changing classification outputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested local sharpness measures depend on parameterization and training duration even when classification behavior is unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: Flatness correlates with function prior in a Boolean system evaluated over its entire input space.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local flatness and function prior correlate among frequently found functions in the tested Boolean network.

record.problems: The principal result rows are qualitative descriptions of scatter or correlation, with no coefficients, error bars, or p-values stated. Generalization variation is induced with incorrectly labelled attack sets, not a natural-label/random-label comparison. Several conditions use binarized or restricted classification tasks and relatively small training sets. The ResNet50/Adam experiment could not reach zero training error for attack sets larger than 2500, so those conditions are excluded.
record.rows_left_out: The text describes the correlation between log P(f) and generalization as excellent or tight in Figures 3–4, but it is outside the versions listed and no claim-version row is retained for it. Figure-only temporal results on parameter rescaling and sharpness trends are not separately extracted because they do not directly measure a listed version. Appendix figures S13–S16 repeat Hessian-based correlation patterns across overtraining; retained representative SGD/Adam descriptions in R8–R11 rather than duplicating each metric/figure. No numerical correlation values are given in those plots.

untested.parts: No matched natural-label versus fixed-random-label training and held-out accuracy comparison.
No width sweep beyond the width required to interpolate.
No controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error comparison or intervention on local connectivity.

No learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning comparison, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, or language benchmark. The text supplies no numerical estimate of the Adam–SGD performance difference.
No held-out performance comparison across batch sizes under a fixed epoch budget or adapted training recipes.

No evaluation of the specified magnitude-aware training-error tolerance or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Appendix A.2 explicitly says the Jiang et al. measure is not directly comparable.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence followed by retraining.

missing.what: Add the direct Adam-versus-plain-SGD held-out performance comparison: the authors report no significant difference with default TensorFlow hyperparameters. Record the qualitative null without inventing numerical differences or a statistical test.
missing.locator: Section 5.3, paragraph following Figure 4; FCN/MNIST and FCN/CIFAR-10 conditions

record.verdict_notes: All judgments use the supplied text. The none-linked rows receive cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; their reported loose or broken correlations remain valid findings about other measures. Attack sets deliberately vary generalization, so they do not supply V1's random-label comparison. Section 5.3's direct optimizer performance statement supplies the limited V4 test.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of natural labels with fixed random labels or their respective held-out accuracies.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures for test error.
The study compares optimizer-specific flatness–generalization correlations, but does not test whether adaptive optimizers have worse held-out performance than SGD under limited tuning.
The study measures Keskar-style sharpness, not magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, and does not compare against norm- and margin-based measures as stated in V7.
No removal of memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: Adam versus plain SGD with default TensorFlow hyperparameters on FCN/binarized MNIST and FCN/car-versus-cat CIFAR-10, using attack sets
relationships.reason: Based on Section 5.3 rather than an extracted row: the authors explicitly report no significant generalization difference from plain SGD. This is a local counterexample under minimal tuning, not a refutation of V4's 'often' qualification.
relationships.display_finding: The authors report no significant generalization difference between Adam and plain SGD with default hyperparameters, but the comparison remains unverified.
